touches.summary: Would limit point (iii) to top-level domain name registries and add providers of European Digital Identity Wallets and of European Business Wallets to the services covered whatever the size of the entity.
Would insert a new paragraph bringing owners, managers and operators of strategic dual-use infrastructure into scope whatever their size.

Would tie essential status in Annex I sectors to the ceilings for small mid-cap enterprises, add wallet providers to point (b) in place of DNS service providers, and add operators of strategic dual-use infrastructure as essential entities.
Would replace the list of details entities give for the national list, adding their main and other establishments in the Union, any representative and their European Business Wallet address.

Would have the Commission assess regularly whether sector implementing acts are needed, and would stop Member States adding further technical, methodological or sector requirements where such an implementing act exists.

Would have the Commission require ransomware details in notifications (whether an attack was detected, its attack vector, any mitigation) and let the CSIRT or competent authority ask whether a ransom was demanded or paid, how much and to whom.
Would add air carriers, placing them under the Member State whose licensing authority granted their operating licence.

Would require every essential or important entity established outside the Union to designate a representative, with electronic communications providers placed under the Member State where they provide services.

touches.summary: Would require significant incidents to be notified through a single-entry point that ENISA would build and run.
Would add a paragraph under which a manufacturer's severe incident report under the Cyber Resilience Act counts as reporting under Article 23(4) where it holds the required information.
Would limit notification to breaches likely to result in a high risk, extend the time limit from 72 to 96 hours and send notifications through the single-entry point.
Would keep direct notification to the supervisory authority until the single-entry point is in place.
Would have the European Data Protection Board propose a common notification template and a list of high-risk cases, reviewed at least every three years.
Would require major ICT-related incidents to be reported through the single-entry point.
Would send voluntary notifications of significant cyber threats through the single-entry point.
Would require critical entities to notify incidents through the single-entry point.
Would let the Commission adopt implementing acts on the type and format of the information notified.
